verdict: Ghostwalk is buildable and demoable by 14:30 IST: every pinned npm version exists with a consistent peer-dependency chain (three 0.186.1 satisfies postprocessing's "<0.187"), the HF parquet mirror downloads in 6 s (HTTP 200, 7,156,732 B, PAR1, 1,067,371 rows) and both fallbacks resolve anonymously (Kaggle 206 via signed GCS URL; xlsx mirror 45,622,278 B), the static-site deployment has no cold-start or key risk, and all three 4.2 must-haves plus all three watch-outs are covered by the design. The refutation is about the numbers, not the stack: I re-ran their exact prep pipeline on November 2011 and simulated their exact 6x2x10 geometry with Held-Karp (k<=8) + NN/2-opt routing. Random (seed 42) -> ABC saves only 14.1% in-sample / 14.2% held-out (98.3 -> 84.5 km on 1-15 Nov; 108.8 -> 93.3 km on 16-30 Nov), not the "-30%" and "Ghost 18.4 km / You 12.9 km" written into the demo script. Good news hidden inside: a 400-move annealing from ABC already gives a further -4.7% in-sample and -3.2% held-out, so "SA beats ABC" is real and survives the split. Secondary risks are concrete and fixable: three stack versions were published today (vite 8.3.5, motion 14.5.0, lucide-react 1.61.0), `typescript@latest` now resolves to 7.0.2, drei DragControls cannot drag InstancedMesh instances, the Held-Karp DP must use typed arrays or the "<1 s month re-score" claim fails, the HF parquet stores every column as string, and the explain-line-by-line requirement is the weakest link for a ~5k-LOC overnight agent build. None of this sinks the entry; all of it must be fixed before the pitch deck is written.
weaknesses: HEADLINE GAIN OVERSTATED: on the proposed geometry (6 aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays, 1.2 m pitch, 4.5 m aisle pitch, dock 3 m from aisle 1; dock->nearest slot 5.1 m, farthest 38.4 m) Random seed 42 = 98.3 km (opt half, 1,130 orders) / 108.8 km (test half, 1,229 orders); ABC = 84.5 km / 93.3 km, i.e. -14.1% / -14.2%. Seeds 1-3 give 98.2-99.7 km, so this is not a seed artefact. The demo script's '-30%' ghost race, 'Ghost 18.4 km / You 12.9 km' and 'XX h' tiles are fiction; the floor is 83% full (100 SKUs in 120 slots) and orders average 7.2 stops across 6 aisles, so slotting has little room to matter. Walking share of time is 46% in this model (74.7 m/order at 1.2 m/s vs 72 s of picking), consistent with the Tompkins hook, but the ghost race will visibly diverge by ~1/7, not ~1/3.

SA BUDGET: a swap touches ~2 x 85 = ~170 orders in the opt half (mean top-100 SKU has 170 picks/month, top SKU 23084 has 487). Python cost was 36.8 ms/move with Held-Karp<=8 + NN/2-opt; a JS proxy will land at ~1-3 ms/move, i.e. only 3k-10k moves in the 10 s live run. That is enough to polish ABC (400 moves already gave -4.7%) but NOT enough to climb from Random to beat ABC on stage. If the live run starts from Random, the 'AI opponent' may lose to the baseline in front of the judges.

HELD-KARP IMPLEMENTATION RISK: 13.4% of covered orders (316 of 2,359) have >12 lines (max 76); 9.3% have >15. Orders with k = 9-12 are ~15%. A Map/object-keyed DP at k = 12 costs 50-100 ms per order in JS, which would make the '<1 s whole-month re-score' and the '300 ms after a judge move' claims false. It must be a flat Float32Array[(1<<k) * k] DP with precomputed Float32Array all-pairs (73 nodes, not the '121 nodes' stated: 1 dock + 6 x (10 bays + 2 ends); stops must be deduplicated to bay nodes before routing).

DAY-ZERO DEPENDENCIES: vite 8.3.5 (published 2026-10-21 06:38 UTC), motion 14.5.0 (2026-10-21 04:35 UTC) and lucide-react 1.61.0 (today) are hours old; react 19.3.1 and @react-three/fiber 9.8.2 are both 2026-10-14. `npm i -D typescript` resolves to 7.0.2 (native TS), not the 5.9 assumed. The idea says vitest 'latest 4.x' but latest is 5.0.5 (4.1.12 is the last 4.x; both accept vite ^8 and need Node >=22). Vite 8 is the rolldown-based line; @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2 requires vite ^8 and Node ^20.19||>=22.12.

HF MIRROR QUIRKS: vancevo/online-retail-ii has an empty README and NO license tag; every column is string-typed (Quantity '12', Price '6.95', InvoiceDate '2009-12-01 07:45:00', Customer_ID string). prep.py must cast with pd.to_numeric/pd.to_datetime (0 unparsable dates, verified). Licence and citation must point to UCI id 502 (CC BY 4.0), with the mirror named only as the transport.

DRAG-AND-DROP: drei DragControls wraps individual Object3D children (`<DragControls><mesh/></DragControls>`) and exposes autoTransform/axisLock/dragLimits/onDrag*; it has no instance or snap support. Dragging an InstancedMesh instance needs a spawned proxy mesh on pointerdown plus custom snap-to-bay. Budget 1 h or cut; click-click swap is correctly the primary path.

JUDGE-TRACKPAD SEGMENT (2:40-3:10): 30 s of a 300 s demo handed to a stranger manipulating 3D on an unfamiliar trackpad; a fumble costs the Ghost Race and SA beats. Also at 1x the first replayed order takes ~62 s (74.7 m at 1.2 m/s), but the whole replay segment is 55 s and '20 orders at 20x' alone needs ~62 s.

EXPLAINABILITY LOAD: 25 agent-hours of TS (sim core, Held-Karp, SA with inverted index, R3F instancing, worker bridge, zustand, SVG minimap, eval script) merged overnight by two sleeping humans who must then explain it line by line in Q&A. The stretch list (batching, congestion, S-shape, Or-opt, affinity overlay, dark-store preset, ablation toggle) doubles the surface they must own.

SCHEDULE ALREADY SLIPPING: machine clock reads 22:26 IST while the build plan's first checkpoint is '22:00 repo init + first commit'; the hourly-commit rule counts only pushed commits (agent branches must push, not just commit locally).

COVERAGE IS LOW AND MUST BE OWNED: top-100 SKUs cover 21.2% of product lines (17,037 of 80,3xx); 350 covered orders (14.8%) become single-line, 85.2% keep >=2 lines. Fine for the brief ('top ~100'), but the Data card must show these numbers or a judge will compute them.
